title: A finite Smith–Toda complex V(4) at the prime 1009

issues.location: Appendix A.2 (filtered binary pairing), description of the box-product map
issues.description: Exposition only. The map T^a(Z1)∧T^b(Z2)→T^{a+b+1}(Z3) is first described as concatenating the BP blocks, and then as multiplying the overlapping factors. The cited standard result (Ravenel, Theorem 2.3.3) covers what is needed, so the main theorem does not depend on this wording.
issues.evidence: Appendix text: 'concatenating the two BP blocks and applying f once' versus 'this map multiplies the last factor of the first BP block with the first factor of the second block'.

coverage:
Read every section (framework, cobar preliminaries, lower complexes, May calculation, Frobenius elimination, final obstruction) and skimmed the appendix. Checked by computer (python/sympy, p=1009):
(a) Exhaustive May E_1 monomials at every possible target (qk+1, u_4+k) for k=1..p+3. The result matches the paper's lists exactly: k=1 gives acbB^{p-2} and acybzB^{p-3}; k=2, p-1 and p give the rows of Table may:remaining-table; every other k is empty.
(b) The incoming-source table at (q+1, u_5+1), checked at p=31, where the same structural argument applies. It matches Table may:n5-table.
(c) The source (5,W) and the targets (6+qj, W+δ+j) of the small-stem lemma, j≤1012. Only the four listed monomials occur, and their splitting cohomology is zero (d(acyB), d(acbA) checked by hand).
(d) Lemma low:algebraic-vanishing: every v_n target and every product-cell obstruction bidegree for n≤3 has an empty May page.
(e) The H^1 crossed-homomorphism linear system for the k=p-1 row has rank 8 of 8, so the only cocycle is zero. This holds under both conjugation conventions.
(f) The May filtration values F_*, F_7 and the inequality F_7<F_* at M=3p.
Checked by hand: the v_5 coboundary relation; the σ-specialization and derivation argument for d_{q+1}; the Frobenius and LHS coefficient-filtration differentials (DC^{p-2}↦zC^{p-2}, D^2υ↦2Dυz); the Thom-class P^1 computation and Toda's αβ^p=0 in Y; the symmetric comodule and the explicit boundary F(r,t_1) of b_{10}; the averaging lift and the page bound S=2p^2-4p+7<qp+1; the surjectivity of multiplication by A^N; and the final cofiber identification. Sanity check: running the same averaging argument with γ=β^p gives Toda's classical relation β_1^{p^2-p+1}=0. I did not re-verify the model-categorical details in the appendix.
main_claim: At p=1009 there is a finite p-local spectrum X with BP_*X ≅ BP_*/(p,v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4) as BP_*BP-comodules, generated in degree 0. In other words, the Smith–Toda complex V(4) exists at this prime. It is built as the cofiber of a v_4 self-map on a unital V(3), after showing that v_4 is a permanent cycle in the Adams–Novikov spectral sequence of V(3).
sibling_notes: The sibling paper in family 308, Finite-Smith-Toda-Complexes-at-Varying-Primes (rank 234), was also marked no_gap_found. This paper does the explicit calculation at p=1009. The k=p obstruction (Sym^{p-1}C(α) null map, giving β^{(p-1)^2}γ=0 before page qp+1) is a Toda-style argument, and it correctly reproduces β_1^{p^2-p+1}=0.
